claims.text: The starting material is a single-phase, disordered solid-solution HEA containing at least five elements at no less than 5 atomic percent each.
The starting HEA has a BCC or FCC structure.
Local lattice distortion induced by atomic-size mismatch primarily governs superconductivity in HEAs outside Nb-Ta and Ti-rich systems.
Local lattice distortions modulate the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
Local lattice distortions modulate electron-phonon coupling strength.
Changes in the density of states and electron-phonon coupling control the superconducting transition temperature.
Substitution with elements having more similar atomic radii will reduce overall atomic-size disparity while retaining compositional complexity.
Reducing atomic-size disparity will lower local lattice distortion.
Local lattice distortion or microstrain can be quantified using X-ray diffraction line broadening or EXAFS.
Reduced local lattice distortion produces a more sharply defined electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
A more sharply defined density of states at the Fermi level enhances electron-phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling raises the superconducting transition temperature.
Reduced local lattice distortion results in a sharper superconducting transition.
The modified HEA will have a higher transition temperature than the baseline alloy.
The modified HEA will have a narrower superconducting transition than the baseline alloy.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the alloy remains a single-phase disordered solid solution.
Phase separation or ordering may change the mechanism governing superconductivity.
